title: Colonial age to today
blurb: European empires take most Muslim lands, the caliphate ends, and fifty new states emerge. Today one in four people is Muslim.

events.title: The Sokoto Caliphate
events.what: Usman dan Fodio founds the Sokoto Caliphate, the largest state in Africa at the time.
events.tie: Usman dan Fodio was a Maliki scholar and preacher who called for learning and justice, and his daughter Nana Asma'u taught women across the region.

events.title: Muhammad Ali's Egypt
events.what: Muhammad Ali takes power in Egypt and builds a modern army, schools and factories, nearly independent of the Ottomans.
events.tie: He sent students to Paris with the al-Azhar scholar Rifa'a al-Tahtawi as their imam, opening a long Muslim debate on faith and modern learning.

events.title: Greek independence
events.what: Greeks rise against Ottoman rule, with massacres on both sides. With help from Britain, France and Russia, Greece becomes independent in 1830.
events.tie: It was the first nation to break away from the Ottomans; nationalism would later split the Muslim lands themselves.

events.title: France invades Algeria
events.what: France invades Algeria. Over the next century Britain, France, Russia and the Netherlands rule most Muslims on earth.
events.tie: The scholar Emir Abd al-Qadir led Algeria's resistance for fifteen years and was later honoured for protecting Christians in Damascus in 1860.

events.title: Omar ibn Said writes his life
events.what: Omar ibn Said, a scholar from Senegal enslaved in North Carolina, writes his life story in Arabic. He begins it with Surat al-Mulk, written from memory.
events.tie: It is the only known autobiography in Arabic by a man enslaved in the United States.

events.title: Emir Abd al-Qadir
events.what: Abd al-Qadir, a young scholar and Sufi, is chosen emir and fights the French for fifteen years. Exiled to Damascus, he shelters thousands of Christians during the riots of 1860.
events.tie: Friends and enemies alike praised him as a model of Islamic honour in war.

events.title: Imam Shamil
events.what: Imam Shamil leads the Muslims of Dagestan and Chechnya against Russia for 25 years. He finally surrenders at Gunib in 1859.
events.tie: Allowed at last to make Hajj, he died in Madinah and is buried in al-Baqi, near the Companions.

events.title: The Tanzimat
events.what: The Ottoman government proclaims the Tanzimat, the reordering: one law for Muslims and non-Muslims, with new courts, schools and a new army.
events.tie: It opened a debate among Muslim scholars and statesmen, still alive today, on how to modernise without losing the sharia.

events.title: The last Mughal
events.what: The Indian uprising fails. Britain exiles the last Mughal emperor to Burma and rules India directly.
events.tie: After 1857 Indian Muslims founded the Deoband seminary (1866) and the Aligarh college (1875) to keep faith and learning alive under British rule.

events.title: Deoband
events.what: After the failed uprising of 1857, scholars found a madrasa in the small town of Deoband to keep Islamic learning alive under British rule. Thousands of schools now follow its model.
events.tie: With the Mughals gone, scholars rather than kings became the keepers of Islam in India.

events.title: Russia takes Central Asia
events.what: Russian armies take Samarkand, and the emir of Bukhara becomes the tsar's vassal. The old cities of Central Asia's scholars come under Russian rule.
events.tie: The homeland of al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi stayed under Russian and then Soviet rule until 1991.

events.title: The Suez Canal
events.what: The Suez Canal opens. Egypt's debts hand it to Britain, which occupies the country in 1882.
events.tie: Pilgrims to Makkah now came by steamship through the canal, and the Hajj grew larger than ever before.

events.title: The Aceh War
events.what: The Netherlands invades Aceh. The Acehnese fight back for over thirty years, one of the longest colonial wars in history.
events.tie: Scholars led much of the resistance and preached it as a jihad to defend the land.

events.title: Aligarh
events.what: Sayyid Ahmad Khan opens a college in Aligarh to teach Muslims modern science and English alongside their faith. It grows into Aligarh Muslim University.
events.tie: Deoband and Aligarh, founded nine years apart, were two answers to one question: how should Muslims live under foreign rule?

events.title: The Firmest Handhold
events.what: In Paris, al-Afghani and his student Muhammad Abduh publish al-Urwa al-Wuthqa, a journal calling Muslims to unite and reform against European rule.
events.tie: Its name, 'the firmest handhold', is taken from the Quran.
events.note: It ran for only eighteen issues but was read from Morocco to India.

events.title: The Mahdi of Sudan
events.what: Muhammad Ahmad, who declared himself the Mahdi in 1881, takes Khartoum from the British-backed Egyptians. His state lasts until British guns destroy it at Omdurman in 1898.
events.tie: Most scholars rejected his claim: the hadith describe the true Mahdi by signs he did not fulfil.

events.title: The Hejaz Railway
events.what: The Hejaz Railway links Damascus to Madinah, paid for by Muslims worldwide. The Hajj journey drops from forty days to four.
events.tie: The line was built for pilgrims; raids in the First World War cut it, and its station in Madinah still stands as a museum.

events.title: The First World War
events.what: The Ottomans join the First World War on Germany's side. Britain backs an Arab revolt in 1916 and promises Palestine to Zionists in 1917.
events.tie: The war ended Ottoman rule over Makkah, Madinah and Jerusalem, and its treaties drew the borders of most of today's Arab states.

events.title: Sykes-Picot
events.what: Britain and France secretly agree to divide the Arab lands of the Ottoman empire between them, while Britain promises the Arabs independence.
events.tie: The borders of Syria, Iraq, Lebanon and Jordan grew out of this deal.

events.title: Balfour and Jerusalem
events.what: Britain's Balfour Declaration promises a Jewish national home in Palestine. Five weeks later British troops enter Jerusalem.
events.tie: Jerusalem, the first qibla and the city of the Night Journey, left Muslim rule after four centuries of Ottoman government.

events.title: The caliphate is abolished
events.what: The new Turkish republic abolishes the caliphate. For the first time since 632 there is no caliph.
events.tie: Muslims from India to Egypt had campaigned to keep the caliphate, through India's Khilafat Movement, and held conferences on reviving it afterwards.

events.title: The Grand Mosque of Paris
events.what: The Grand Mosque of Paris opens, built to honour the Muslim soldiers from France's colonies who died for France in the First World War.
events.tie: Muslims are now the largest religious minority in France and much of Western Europe.
events.note: Stories that the mosque hid Jews during the Second World War are widely told; how many it saved is debated.

events.title: The Muslim Brotherhood
events.what: A young schoolteacher, Hasan al-Banna, founds the Muslim Brotherhood in Ismailia. It becomes one of the most influential Islamic movements of the century.
events.tie: It spread through schools, charity and preaching; governments have by turns tolerated it, banned it and fought it.

events.title: Saudi Arabia
events.what: The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia is proclaimed. Oil is found six years later.
events.tie: The new kingdom took charge of Makkah, Madinah and the Hajj, which has grown from tens of thousands of pilgrims to millions.

events.title: Oil in Arabia
events.what: Oil is struck at Dammam Well No. 7. Arabia's economy, and the world's, changes for good.
events.tie: Oil wealth paid for roads, airports and the vast expansions of the Grand Mosque in Makkah and the Prophet's Mosque in Madinah.

events.title: Indonesia
events.what: Sukarno proclaims Indonesia's independence from the Dutch. After four years of war it is free. Today it has more Muslims than any other country.
events.tie: Islam came to these islands mostly through traders and teachers, not conquest.

events.title: Partition and Pakistan
events.what: British India is partitioned. Pakistan is born as a homeland for Muslims; a million die in the migrations.
events.tie: Founded as a homeland for India's Muslims, Pakistan became one of the largest Muslim nations, while millions of Muslims also stayed in India.

events.title: The Nakba
events.what: Israel is declared. Over 700,000 Palestinians are expelled or flee. Palestinians call it the Nakba, the catastrophe.
events.tie: Palestine holds al-Aqsa, where the Prophet ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey (17:1), so the events of 1948 touched Muslims everywhere.

events.title: Widening the Haram
events.what: Saudi Arabia begins the first great modern expansion of the Masjid al-Haram. Later rebuilding lets millions pray around the Kaaba at once.
events.tie: Almost every age has widened the Mosque, from the caliph Umar's time to the Ottomans.

events.title: The year of independence
events.what: Seventeen African states gain independence in one year. Algeria follows in 1962 after an eight-year war.
events.tie: Many of the new states, like Senegal, Mali, Niger, Somalia and Mauritania, were Muslim-majority, and Islam shaped their national life.

events.title: The recorded Quran
events.what: Mahmoud Khalil al-Husary records the whole Quran in slow, careful recitation. Records, tapes and radio carry it into homes around the world.
events.tie: For the first time, anyone anywhere could learn recitation from a master reciter's voice.
events.note: It is widely described as the first complete recorded murattal recitation.

events.title: Algeria free
events.what: After a war of almost eight years in which hundreds of thousands die, Algeria wins independence, 132 years after the French invasion.
events.tie: Islam was the banner of the resistance; Algerians call their country the land of a million and a half martyrs.

events.title: Malcolm X at Hajj
events.what: Malcolm X makes Hajj and writes home that he has seen pilgrims of every colour living as brothers. He returns as El-Hajj Malik El-Shabazz.
events.tie: Hajj puts every race and nation in the same two white cloths, as the Farewell Sermon taught.

events.title: The Six-Day War
events.what: In six days Israel takes East Jerusalem, the West Bank, Gaza, Sinai and the Golan. Al-Aqsa comes under occupation.
events.tie: Al-Aqsa, the first qibla of Muslims, came under Israeli control, while its daily running stayed with an Islamic trust, the Waqf.

events.title: The OIC
events.what: After an arson attack on al-Aqsa, Muslim states found the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation. Today it has 57 members.

events.title: The Iranian revolution
events.what: Revolution topples the Shah and makes Iran an Islamic republic. The same year the Soviets invade Afghanistan.
events.tie: It was the first modern revolution made in the name of Islam, and it renewed debates among Muslims everywhere about religion and the state.

events.title: Hajj by air
events.what: Jeddah's Hajj Terminal opens, a field of tent-shaped roofs built for pilgrims arriving by air. Journeys that once took months now take hours.
events.tie: In the 1950s about 100,000 pilgrims a year came from abroad; by 2019 nearly two and a half million performed Hajj.
events.note: Pilgrim numbers follow Saudi official figures and are approximate.

events.title: Printing the Quran
events.what: The King Fahd Complex in Madinah starts printing the Quran. It now prints millions of copies a year in dozens of languages.

events.title: Central Asia independent
events.what: The Soviet Union collapses. Six Muslim-majority republics from Azerbaijan to Kyrgyzstan become independent states.
events.tie: In the lands of Imam al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi, mosques reopened and Muslims could study and practise Islam openly after seventy years of Soviet restriction.

events.title: Srebrenica
events.what: Bosnian Serb forces overrun the UN 'safe area' of Srebrenica and kill more than 8,000 Bosniak Muslim men and boys. International courts rule it genocide.
events.tie: The worst mass killing in Europe since the Second World War, against Muslims whose ancestors accepted Islam under the Ottomans.

events.title: 9/11 and the wars
events.what: The 9/11 attacks. The United States invades Afghanistan, then Iraq in 2003. Two decades of war follow.
events.tie: Muslim scholars worldwide condemned the attacks, recalling the Quran's teaching that killing one innocent soul is like killing all humanity (5:32).

events.title: The Arab Spring
events.what: A street vendor's protest in Tunisia sparks uprisings across the Arab world. Four rulers fall; Syria descends into war.
events.tie: Millions took to the streets across the Arab world, and its wars, above all in Syria, drove one of the largest refugee movements of modern times.

events.title: The Rohingya
events.what: A military crackdown in Myanmar drives more than 700,000 Rohingya Muslims into Bangladesh. The camps at Cox's Bazar become among the largest on earth.
events.tie: Muslims have lived in Arakan, on the Bay of Bengal, for centuries.

events.title: Two billion Muslims
events.what: Around two billion Muslims, one in four people on earth. Every year millions stand at Arafat where the farewell sermon was given.
